name: Antimetabolite DMARDs
summary: Methotrexate is an immunosuppressant used for inflammatory conditions such as rheumatoid arthritis, psoriasis and Crohn's disease, and sometimes for cancer. The NHS says it calms the immune system and helps reduce inflammation.
mechanism: Methotrexate blocks an enzyme called dihydrofolate reductase, which the body uses to make tetrahydrofolate, a form of folate needed to build DNA and RNA. In inflammatory conditions, how low-dose methotrexate works is less clear.
cautions: Taking it daily by mistake instead of weekly has caused overdoses that were sometimes fatal.
The MHRA introduced new measures in 2020 to reduce this risk, including a patient card for oral products.
Regular blood tests are used to monitor treatment.
The NHS says methotrexate is not recommended in pregnancy because it can cause birth defects.

classInteractions.with: NSAIDs such as ibuprofen, aspirin and naproxen
classInteractions.effect: NSAIDs can increase the risk of methotrexate toxicity, so they are used only on specialist advice.

source.title: NHS Specialist Pharmacy Service: Managing interactions with methotrexate

classInteractions.effect: Trimethoprim and co-trimoxazole are advised against because of the risk of severe bone marrow suppression.

source.title: NHS Specialist Pharmacy Service: Managing interactions with methotrexate

classInteractions.effect: Live vaccines are not recommended during treatment.
